title: VOSK, H. — PRIVATE CHAMBERS, THE ADAMANT CROWN
intro:
Six hours ago a servant of the Adamant Crown found the door to these chambers sealed from the inside and Hadrian Vosk on the floor behind it.

You were his Interrogator for eleven years. Ninety minutes ago you were handed his rosette in front of witnesses. Inquisitor Crase was kind about it. The verdict was written before the body cooled.

The medicae are outside with a gurney and a schedule. They will give you eight minutes.

Type HELP if you need the verb list. Nothing in this room will highlight itself for you.
look:
His chambers. You have stood here a thousand times and it has never been this quiet.

The BODY is on the floor between the desk and the side table, the autopistol still in the right hand. The DESK is clear except for a blotter, an ink-stained PAGE, a desk CALENDAR and his NOTEBOOK. On the side table, a regicide BOARD, mid-game. The SHUTTER on the west window is open — which it never is. By the door, the seal-integrity REGISTER blinks its little green rune at nobody.
look_no_body:
His chambers, emptier by one man.

The DESK: blotter, ink-stained PAGE, desk CALENDAR, his NOTEBOOK. On the side table, the regicide BOARD, mid-game, exactly as it was. The SHUTTER stands open four degrees. By the door, the seal-integrity REGISTER.

The outline they chalked is procedural and means nothing. You keep looking at it anyway.
body_removed:
The medicae come in at the eighth minute, apologise, and take him.

They are not unkind and they are not going to argue with a rosette that is ninety minutes old. The senior one says "Throne keep him, sir," and means it, and then the door closes and the room is just furniture.

Whatever you did not read off him, you will not be reading.

They are taking him down to the medicae deck on tier one. Ostro will have him open inside the hour, and Sergeant Oduya will go with him, because nobody has told her not to.

objects.careless: Hadrian Vosk, two hundred and eighty-seven years of service, on the floor of his own chambers with his own pistol in his own hand. There is very little blood. His face is doing nothing at all.
objects.careful:
The grip-angle is wrong for a man in despair and right for a man being careful — wrist braced against the desk leg, elbow set, the way he taught you to brace a pict-recorder. He did not want to miss and make a mess for somebody to clean.

His BOOTS are on the wrong feet.

objects.careless: His boots are on the wrong feet. Left on right, right on left. The medicae will write "distress" and nobody will ever question it.
objects.careful:
Both boots laced evenly, tension matched, tongues straight. No sock displacement. The bootjack has been used and returned to the wall — in the wrong orientation for a right-handed man in a hurry.

He sat down. He took his time. He did this last.

Sarrow's Reach. Eleven years ago, your first field posting, still a records-adept, across a table from the Governor's people with a manifest in front of you that you both knew was forged and neither of you could say so. At the rest-halt he came back with his boots swapped and held your eye exactly as long as it took.

Read it backwards.

You never discussed it. It has never been written down by anyone, which is precisely why it is the only language he had left.

objects.careless: A regicide board, mid-game. Vosk played constantly and badly and would not be told. Black is losing.
objects.careful:
Three pieces cannot legally stand where they stand.

A second white Emperor on D2 — there is only ever one. A black Lexicanum on F4, a light square, and the Lexicanum is dark-bound. A white Sentinel on C9, the far rank, unpromoted, where promotion is compulsory.

Three errors is not a bad player. Three errors is a man writing.

Cantor regicide notation and Lexicanum Vault shelf-addresses are the same alphabet — the same Administratum office codified both, a nine-by-nine grid over nine levels, and a Vault address is three file-rank pairs: block-and-level, aisle-run, shelf.

In piece-hierarchy order — Emperor, Lexicanum, Sentinel — the board reads D2-F4-C9.

It is an address written in furniture. No cogitator will ever index it.

objects.careless: The west shutter is open. Ninety millimetres. Nobody came through it, and the room was sealed from the inside regardless.
objects.careful:
Four degrees, and fixed — the ratchet shimmed with a folded requisition slip so it cannot drift. Vosk never once opened this shutter in eleven years. He complained about Cantor's light, said it came off the manufactorum stacks the colour of old teeth.

Light in: at the twelfth hour the blade will cross the desk and end at the third drawer. The third drawer is empty, and dusted. It is where the regicide set lives. He is telling you the board is out on the table on purpose.

Sightline out: at the twelfth hour, and only then, the aperture frames one thing across the Crown gap — Transit Gallery 9 of the Choir Spire, and in it the shuttered window of transcription cell four.

A time and a place. Twelfth hour. Cell four.

objects.careless: Ink on the ball of his right thumb. A blank sheet on the blotter. Ash in the censer, still warm. He wrote something and he burned it, and that is the end of that.
objects.careful:
The ink is auto-quill ink, not his pen ink. Vosk wrote longhand out of vanity and thought machines took the character out of a sentence — so using the auto-quill was a decision.

The sheet on the blotter is not blank. It is the second sheet, the impression platen. Illegible, but it carries a strike-count north of nine hundred glyphs on one page, where his longhand fits two hundred. He wrote compressed, in a notation that is not Gothic.

And the unit is a Cael-pattern quill, whose pressure-drum tension log survives the burning of the paper. It gives a duration and a stop-time.

He wrote it, and lit the censer, four minutes before the estimated hour of death.

He knew the minute. A man in despair does not schedule.

objects.careless: A desk calendar. A date six days out is circled. An appointment, presumably, that he is not going to keep.
objects.careful:
Circled with the auto-quill, not his pen — the same sitting as the burned page. Circled twice, one ring inside the other, pressed hard enough to score the leaf beneath.

And under the sheet, on the leaves for previous cycles, the ghosts of erased circles. Same weekday. Every eighty-four days. Back as far as the pad goes.

There is no corresponding entry anywhere. Not the diary, not the adjutant's book, not the cogitator, not the Crown's audience schedule.

An eighty-one-year standing appointment that has never once generated a record, in a hive built entirely for the making of records.

objects.take_text: You put it in your coat. It is heavier than it looks, and it is the only object in this room the archive has never touched.
objects.careless: His notebook. Eleven years of longhand, in a room with a cogitator that would have been four times faster.
objects.careful:
Eleven years. Every case, every name, every sum, in ink, by hand, in a room containing a Cael-pattern cogitator he was issued free and maintained beautifully and appears never to have trusted with a single sentence that mattered.

The last page is a shopping list. Lamp oil. Wax. A tin of the black tea he liked and pretended not to.

That is the tell. The last thing Hadrian Vosk wrote by hand was nothing at all, on the day he wrote nine hundred glyphs into a machine and burned them.

objects.careless: The seal-integrity register by the door. Green rune. The aperture log shows one entry in eleven hours: Sergeant Oduya, forcing it, this morning.
objects.careful:
The aperture log shows one entry. The seal-integrity register is a different instrument and shows a second event.

A warden's seal broken and re-set, cleanly, forty minutes before Bez put her shoulder through the door.

Somebody with a warden's key stood in this room while he was on the floor, and left, and closed it behind them properly.

objects.careless: His desk. Immaculate. The third drawer is empty and has been dusted.
objects.careful: Empty, dusted, and lined with the felt cut-out that a regicide set sits in. The set is on the side table. He took it out and left the drawer clean, which is not what a man does with a game he is in the middle of.

A1.label: Three illegal pieces on the board — a Vault shelf-address in furniture: D2-F4-C9
A1.file_text: FILED. CLASS: SCENE DETAIL / RECREATIONAL EFFECTS. INDEXED. REQUISITION-ELIGIBLE.
A1.refusal:
You write the code in your notebook and the terminal, quite reasonably, will not let you requisition against a shelf-address you have only told your coat about. The Vault indexes filings. To pull the shelf you must first hand the shelf to the archive.

You notice the shape of that and file it anyway.

A2.label: Shutter fixed at four degrees — twelfth hour, cell four, the emptied third drawer
A2.file_text: FILED. CLASS: SCENE DETAIL / VENTILATION ANOMALY. INDEXED.
A2.note_text: Written down. Twelfth hour. Cell four. Third drawer emptied on purpose.

A3.label: The boots were swapped deliberately — Sarrow's Reach. Read it backwards.
A3.note_text:
You write it down in your own hand: BOOTS — SARROW'S REACH — HE MEANS REVERSE IT.

It takes eleven words and it is the most important thing in your coat.
A3.refusal:
The filing template opens. It offers three classifications for the condition of a body's footwear.

    [1] DISTRESS
    [2] DISORDER
    [3] SELF-NEGLECT

There is no fourth option. There is no free-text field. There is nowhere on this form to say that a dead man is speaking to you in a private language from a rest-halt on Sarrow's Reach eleven years ago.

You close the template. Some things only fit in a notebook.

A4.label: Auto-quill entry: 900+ glyphs, non-Gothic, written and burned four minutes before death
A4.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: SCENE DETAIL / DESTROYED DOCUMENT.
DRUM TENSION LOG EXTRACTED — STOP-TIME 0997.4.211 / SIXTEENTH HOUR, 22 MIN.
INDEXED.
A4.note_text: Written down — but the drum log will not read itself onto paper. Without filing the unit you have his handwriting and not his clock.

A5.label: Six days circled twice; ghost circles every 84 days, 81 years, no record anywhere
A5.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: SCENE DETAIL / PERSONAL EFFECTS.
PICT-CAPTURE ATTACHED. INDEXED.
A5.note_text: You copy the ghost circles out by hand, weekday by weekday, back as far as the pad goes. It takes four minutes and it is in ink and it is yours.

A6.label: Vosk kept eleven years of casework in longhand and never trusted the cogitator
A6.note_text: Noted. He did not trust the machine. You are currently standing in front of the machine.
A6.refusal: You could file an observation about a man's stationery preferences. You find you would rather not.

A7.label: A warden's seal broken and re-set 40 minutes before the door was forced
A7.file_text: FILED. CLASS: SCENE SECURITY / SEAL EVENT. INDEXED.
A7.note_text: Written down. Somebody was in here with a key.

A20.label: Dispatch 0997.4-1188 — Vermilion scrub-on-carry, 41 sec, Kesh countersigned in person
A20.note_text:
You copy it out by hand. The ID. The transit authority. The forty-one seconds. The name in the duty-archivist field.

Four separate things, four separate lines, and nothing on the screen suggested you do any of it.

A8.label: The room was staged in advance, in an order, for one specific reader
A8.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: SCENE ASSESSMENT / INVESTIGATOR FINDING. INDEXED. REQUISITION-ELIGIBLE.

It is the most useful thing you have. Crase can act on it. Clerks who were sullen this morning will fetch things for you this afternoon, because a filed finding is a finding the Crown has heard of.

It is also, now, a document stating that the deceased anticipated his own death and left instructions, held in an archive, in a hive where somebody arranged for him to die.
A8.note_text: You keep it in your coat, which means it is not a finding. It is a feeling you happen to have written down, and no clerk in this Crown will fetch you so much as a chair on the strength of it.

A22.label: The Case Précis — the record's own account of your day, in four true sentences
A22.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: CASE PRÉCIS / COUNTERSIGNED. INDEXED.

It was already there. Filing it files a copy of the thing you were shown, into the place it came from, which the cogitator accepts without remark because a document being filed twice is not an error.

You now hold, in the archive, the archive's account of your day. That is what everybody else will read.
A22.note_text:
You copy the four paragraphs out by hand, in full, before you do anything else with them.

It takes twenty minutes and your hand aches at the end of it and it is the single most useful twenty minutes of the entire act, because in eleven days this document will say something else and you will be the only person in the sector who can prove it used to say this.

strings.body_gone: They took him at the eighth minute. Whatever was on him is a medicae photograph now.
strings.read_room_locked:
The verb is there. It has been there since you walked in, greyed and unremarked, and it will not do anything yet.

Three of the signs. You have fewer than three.
strings.read_room_prompt:
You stop moving and let the room assemble itself.

READ ROOM FORWARD  — take the signs in the order he set them down
READ ROOM BACKWARD — take them the other way
strings.crase_rescue:
The terminal accepts D2-F4-C9 and begins composing a formal Inquisitorial requisition — seal, priority, the full apparatus — against two centuries of Munitorum drainage ledgers, addressed to the office of the Lord-Prefect.

A hand comes over the back of your chair and one finger rests on the arrest-key.

"Not into Kesh's clerks, love. They'll frame it."

Crase does not laugh at you. She fixes it herself, quietly, reverses the pairs like it is a typo anyone might make, and never mentions it again.

It is the warmest thing anyone does for you today.
strings.vault_none:
LEXICANUM VAULT :: NO SUCH SHELF-ADDRESS IN THIS BLOCK.
CHECK QUERY.
strings.no_one_here: There is nobody here to ask. This is the one room in the Crown with nobody in it, which was your request, and which was granted instantly, which was a kindness.
strings.body_removed_elsewhere:
Somewhere above you, at the eighth minute, the medicae take him.

You are not there. Nobody sends word, because nobody has been told to, and the first you will know of it is the empty floor.

He will be on tier one within the hour.

exits.text:
You take the lift down to tier four.

Behind you the medicae are still waiting with their gurney and their schedule, and they will not wait for you, and both of you know it.

exits.blocked:
He is still on the floor of this room and the medicae are still outside with a gurney and a schedule.

There is nothing on tier one to look at yet, and Sergeant Oduya is not going anywhere while he is in here.
exits.text:
Bez takes you out through the door on the way down, and does it physically, because she has been waiting six hours for somebody to let her.

Here is where she stood. Here is the strike-plate. Here is where the splinters went, and they went inward, and she puts your hand on the frame so that you can feel that they did.

"Eleven hours," she says. "Twelfth to the twenty-third."

Then the lift, nine tiers down, in silence, with her shoulder against the wall.
One floor down, to the office of a man who has been cross-checking a tithe variance since the fourth hour and is not, by any measure available to him, having a bad day.

exits.blocked:
The Choir Spire is across the Crown gap and holds four hundred vessels in nine galleries, and you have no idea which of them you would be walking up there to ask about.

You need a cell, or an hour, or a reason. You have none of the three.
exits.text:
Across the Crown gap by transit bridge, and up.

The Choir Spire is the only structure on this world taller than the Adamant Crown and it is the only one nobody looks at, because looking at it means thinking about what is in it.

revisit: His chambers. The Crown has them for another few hours and then it takes them back.
